name: Aryanism
summary: Aryanism holds that an 'Aryan' race, narrowed by Nazi theorists to Nordic or Germanic peoples, is biologically superior, created human culture and is entitled to rule other races. It treats race mixing as the cause of civilizational decline, races as locked in a natural struggle, and the state as an instrument for preserving racial purity, with Jews cast as the chief enemy.
scope: Racial Aryanism as developed from Gobineau and Chamberlain through Nazi theorists (Gunther, Rosenberg, Hitler's Mein Kampf) and carried on by post-1945 neo-Nazis. Excludes the older philological meaning of 'Aryan' and the Indo-Aryan peoples, and Italian fascist 'Mediterranean' variants. Economic and religious questions are mostly unaddressed by the racial doctrine and answered low-confidence from Nazi practice.

keyFigures.name: Arthur de Gobineau
keyFigures.role: Author of the Essay on the Inequality of the Human Races, an early theorist of Aryan superiority.

keyFigures.name: Hans F. K. Gunther
keyFigures.role: Nazi-era racial theorist who ranked European subtypes with Nordics highest.

keyFigures.name: Adolf Hitler
keyFigures.role: Author of Mein Kampf and leader of the regime that applied Aryanism as state policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Hitler treats the state as a racial organism rather than an economic mechanism, which subordinates markets to the race, though no market doctrine is stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Aryanism as a racial doctrine is indifferent to ownership; the Nazi regime kept private property under state direction rather than nationalizing broadly.

unions-good.rationale: Hitler attacks Marxism and its labor organizations as Jewish instruments, and independent unions were dissolved under Nazism.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No racial-doctrine position; the Nazi state directed business toward national-racial ends but adherents differ.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-state powers against designated enemies fit the Nazi order, though not a racial-doctrine point.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents promote open racial hatred and see such restrictions as Jewish-influenced censorship; the Nazi regime itself restricted speech only against its enemies.

strong-leader.rationale: Hitler dismisses parliamentary mediocrity and puts personality and a leader first; Nazism rested on the Fuhrer principle.

state-harmful.rationale: Hitler describes the state as an essential biological instrument for preserving and advancing the race.

empower-police-military.rationale: Racial struggle, conquest and enforcement of racial laws required a strong military and police apparatus.

decide-locally.rationale: Racial unity under a central state and leader is the aim; Nazism centralized power in the Reich.

traditional-family.rationale: Nazi policy promoted the racially fit family as the reproductive base of the race, though Hitler's text excerpt says little on family.

abortion-legal.rationale: Nazi policy banned abortion for Aryan women while forcing it on others; population and race policy, not individual choice, governs.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents split between Christian, pagan and anti-Christian strands; Gobineau was Christian while Nazi leaders were mixed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents reject equal treatment of races and see race mixing and racial equality as harmful; Nazism institutionalized racial injustice.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Hitler argues racial purity is the precondition of cultural capacity and that Aryans created culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Nazism sought radical racial transformation rather than gradual change; not a doctrinal point of Aryanism itself.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Racial purity requires keeping non-Aryans out; neo-Nazi Western Imperium visions limit full citizenship to Aryans.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The race-nation ordering and Nazi aggression rejected supranational limits on racial states.

nation-first.rationale: Racial interest and survival come first; Nazism pursued conquest for Aryan Germans without regard for global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Universal human-rights intervention contradicts racial hierarchy; adherents reject equal moral worth.

open-borders.rationale: Mixing between races is held to cause decline, so open borders contradict the core doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nazism and its successors sought a radical racial revolution, though through legal seizure of power in Germany.

experts-over-public.rationale: Racial science claimed expert authority, but Nazism also rested on leader and instinct over technocracy.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nazi autarkic economics favored protection; not a point of racial doctrine.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Blood-and-soil romanticism favored peasant farmers, but this is not core to Aryanism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxist abolition of money is rejected as Jewish-inspired by Hitler's anti-Marxism.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nazi Germany replaced unions with state-run labor bodies, but this is regime practice rather than Aryan doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hitler's rejection of parliamentary democracy and the Nazi one-party state; neo-Nazi visions are also autocratic.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Gobineau was a Legitimist while Nazism was not monarchist; adherents are split.

democracy-best.rationale: Hitler dismisses parliamentary democracy as weak and mediocre; Gobineau opposed democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Hitler favors personality and leadership over mass voting; plebiscites were used by the regime for acclamation only.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a Marxist idea that Hitler denounces.

natural-rulers.rationale: Core claim: the Aryan race is a superior group entitled to rule other peoples.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hitler presents struggle as natural law and rejects pacifism; Nazism used violence at scale.

war-builds-character.rationale: Struggle selects the strong in Hitler's account, and Nazi theory held war between races was destined.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is the instrument preserving the race, so privatizing defense runs against the doctrine.

military-superiority.rationale: Racial struggle and Lebensraum required dominant military force.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Hitler's goal is a German state of the German nation, with the state preserving a racial group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: History is driven by race and racial struggle, not class; Hitler rejects Marxism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The doctrine asserts natural inequality of races and persons; Gobineau's essay rejects equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land belongs to the dominant race in Lebensraum thinking; authority for non-Aryan peoples is not recognised.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Nazi ethos subordinates the individual to the racial community.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Race and nation come before the individual in Nazi theory; Hitler treats the state as serving the race.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Blood-and-soil thought romanticizes nature, but this is not core to Aryanism.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-natalism for the Aryan race and Lebensraum expansion; limits apply only to the 'unfit'.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nazism claimed to renew the race rather than restore the past, while Gobineau lamented decline; split.

direct-action.rationale: Nulled: the statement now asks whether direct action should replace electoral politics (reworded 2026-11-10, Codex review). This answer rested on direct action used alongside elections or on a mixed record, which does not support agreeing that it should replace them; its sources need re-reading against the new text.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nazi movement used street violence alongside elections, but this is not core to Aryanism.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Aryan culture-founding is seen as civilizational achievement, hence not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; a stratified order is assumed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution is by racial membership and service; need-based egalitarianism is rejected as Marxist.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Hitler blames Jewish finance rather than owners as such; the Marxist exploitation theory is rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marxism is a central enemy in Hitler's account.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization is Marxist; blood-and-soil favored the independent peasant.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: War flows from racial struggle in this view, not capitalism.

harm-principle.rationale: The state may restrict individuals for racial purposes, as the Nuremberg-era regime did.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights depend on racial membership; the Nazi regime stripped Jews of citizenship.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Anti-democratic racial state; exit as a check contradicts the doctrine.

state-as-business.rationale: Hitler says the state is not an economic mechanism but a racial organism.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Core claim of race theory: ability and culture differ by race through blood.

organic-representation.rationale: Hitler favors a racial community and leader over parties; not a stated corporatist plan in sources.

total-state.rationale: Nazism subjected culture, education and economy to racial aims; the state serves the race.

national-rebirth.rationale: Gobineau's decline narrative and Nazi rhetoric of racial renewal; Hitler cites decay by blood poisoning.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lebensraum and Generalplan Ost expanded territory for Aryans.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Nazi loyalty oaths to the leader fit, but feudal lord-follower rule is not Aryanism.

universal-morality.rationale: The doctrine rejects universal equality; morals are racially grounded.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Aryanism is violently antisemitic; Hitler sees Jews as parasites and lacking culture.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democracy and worker councils are rejected in favor of the leader principle.

rule-by-example.rationale: Nazi rule rested on law, force and propaganda, not example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Each Aryan nation may rule itself, but not other peoples; the claim is racially bounded.

force-without-un.rationale: Nazi Germany used force for racial aims; supranational approval is rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: Mixed: race science claims reason, but Hitler stresses instinct, blood and will.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tradition, feeling, will or reason in general, not religious faith, which this statement now asks about.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benefits are reserved for the racial community; Jews were stripped of citizenship.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hitler rejects Marxist class struggle in favor of national-racial unity.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Aryan cultural achievement is central, so heritage is valued.

workers-nation.rationale: Hitler rejects the international class and wants workers inside a national-racial community.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nazi ideology assigned women a reproductive role in the racial state; Hitler's racial program puts the race's continuity first.

ban-interest.rationale: Hitler attacks Jewish finance, but a legal ban on interest was not a doctrinal demand in sources read.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Nuremberg Laws banned race mixing and removed Jews' citizenship; neo-Nazi visions limit full citizenship to Aryans.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist account of the state is rejected; the state serves the race.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Aryanism denies non-Aryans can assimilate because race, not culture, defines belonging.

elite-replacement.rationale: Modern Aryanist currents hold that Jews and elites engineer racial dilution, matching Hitler's blood-poisoning claims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hitler denounces parliamentary politicians as weak and mediocre.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Aryanism article records the Nazi regime's compulsory sterilization of people deemed hereditarily unfit.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hitler's state actively shapes the race and nation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hitler blames race mixing for the decline of civilizations; Gobineau and Nuremberg-era law agree.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The doctrine ranks races, and Gobineau's essay rejects human equality.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nazism endorsed settlement and displacement in the east; calling it colonial and wrong runs against that, though it could simply be descriptive.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Hitler rejects democratic legitimacy; Aryans are held entitled to rule others.

population-transfer.rationale: Nazism planned removal and murder of Eastern peoples for Lebensraum and forced Jewish emigration.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Hitler presents struggle as natural law; Nazi expansion relied on force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Hitler sees struggle as natural law that selects the strong, and Nazi theory stressed racial war.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Racial rule over others is a core claim; republican freedom is not endorsed.

separated-powers.rationale: Nazi doctrine concentrates authority in the leader; Hitler scorns parliamentary checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Marxist concept; the Nazi party played a similar role but the statement is about the working class.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were banned under Nazi rule, though this is not Aryan doctrine.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Lebensraum arguments tie poverty to land shortage, but not to population as such; split.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Mixing between races is held to cause decline; unity requires racial purity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of rulers by race and leadership, not chance.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Nazi Germany fixed prices, but price control is not a point of racial doctrine and adherents differ.

party-controls-media.rationale: Nazi Germany controlled the press, and Hitler blames Jewish control of the press as the reason.

party-commands-army.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-10): its rationale says party or leader command is not a doctrinal point of the ideology, so the sources cited here do not answer this statement.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nazism subordinated the army to party and leader; not a doctrinal point of Aryanism.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Nazi party discipline was strong, but not a doctrine of Aryanism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Hitler held supreme command and the leader principle places the forces under the leader.

clerical-rule.rationale: Racial leadership, not clergy, rules; Nazi rejection of clerical politics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Hitler treats Marxist defeatism as treason and national struggle as natural.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nazi Germany censored 'degenerate' art and Hitler ties culture to racial purity.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances for conquest were pursued; neither isolation nor alliance is doctrine.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nazism favored a mass military and party militias but not abolition of a professional army.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nazism sought to unite all Germans in one Reich, as its expansion into Austria and the Sudetenland shows.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The doctrine ranks races and claims only Aryans create culture.

death-penalty.rationale: The Nazi state used capital punishment extensively against enemies.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Race science relied on Darwinian struggle language; Gobineau used the Bible but this is not Aryanism proper.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nazi citizenship law (the 1935 Reich Citizenship Law) reserved citizenship for those of German or related blood; the profile's sources describe the Nuremberg race laws.

minority-language-support.rationale: Racial nation-state offers no support to non-Aryan minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The individual is subordinated to the racial community.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Equal moral worth is rejected, so duties to the world's poor are not recognised.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is conditional on membership and service to the racial community, as Jewish property was seized.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Hitler attacks Bolshevism as Jewish; the state-capitalist label is a Marxist-internal debate.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Nazi model made the leader the embodiment of the racial community and abolished parties, not a neutral figurehead.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Racial doctrine does not address tax rates; Nazi fiscal policy was not flat, so this is a weak inference.

character-from-environment.rationale: Aryanism holds that race determines character and ability, so environment cannot alter them.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The leader principle placed the Führer's will above statute, and Mein Kampf rejects constraint by parliamentary law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects democracy and divided power in favour of rule by a leader embodying the racial elite.

leader-cult.rationale: The Führer cult of portraits, mass rallies and praise as embodiment of the nation was central to Nazi practice and doctrine.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Nazi doctrine replaced class struggle with racial struggle and attacked Marxism as a Jewish creation.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Hitler demanded union of all Germans and Lebensraum, and Nazi Germany annexed Austria and the Sudetenland on national grounds.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a league, federation, cooperation or unity in general, not one state, which this statement now asks.

reviewHistory.rationale: Racial doctrine favoured union of Germanic and Nordic peoples across borders as racial kin.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The racial hierarchy denied inferior races any self-governing institutions in the state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Adherents wanted minorities, especially Jews, out of the nation; whether by emigration to a homeland or not is not settled by doctrine.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Hitler explains history by race and blood and treats ideas and economics as secondary.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Nazi ideology assigned women a mainly domestic and maternal role, so parity in public bodies was rejected.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nazi education put race and the Germanic past at the centre of history teaching.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nazi schooling demanded loyalty to the nation and race and to its symbols.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Adherents oppose preferences for minorities but also reject race-blind judgement, since they favour race-conscious policy for Aryans; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Nazi rule suspended civil rights and put the racial community above individual rights.

minority-veto.rationale: Hitler rejected majority rule and the equality of persons but equally rejected any individual veto; the leader decides, so a minority veto is inconsistent.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects parliamentary democracy and majority rule in favour of leader authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Hitler held that Aryans may use and dominate lower creatures and races; animal protection was not central, though Nazi Germany passed animal-welfare laws, so adherents differ.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Aryanism demands that members of the racial community fight and serve the nation, so withdrawal from public life is rejected.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nazi doctrine tied citizenship and public office to racial membership, and the Nuremberg Laws restricted both to those of German blood.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchism over territory lost after 1918 and a Greater Germany were central aims of Nazi policy.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The doctrine holds Aryans as the natural rulers over other races, so rule by non-Aryan descendants is rejected. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Racial Aryanism was the core doctrine of Nazism, the movement that anti-fascist constitutions were written against.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Aryanists reject the equation of Nazism with communism and regard Marxism as a Jewish product.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale argues against its value: it denies the army an independent guardian role, yet gives a positive.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nazi Germany used the army and the SS as instruments of the party and the racial state, but the Wehrmacht was meant to serve the leader; the guardian role was not doctrine.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority rule and parliamentary accountability in favour of leader authority.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Blood-and-soil ideas tie land to the race, but this is not a communal land tenure doctrine; adherents are unspecific.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Hitler attacked parliaments and majority decision, so legislative control of spending is rejected.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Aryanism rests on a racial hierarchy and denies equality between races, so treating unequal outcomes as discrimination is rejected.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nazi racial policy promoted large 'Aryan' families with marriage loans and child bonuses; the cited USHMM page does not itself describe these measures.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Nazi regime ran work-creation programmes for Aryans, but the racial doctrine itself is silent on this.

democratic-peace.rationale: Aryanism holds that races are locked in natural struggle, so democracy and peace are rejected.

non-intervention.rationale: Racial struggle and expansion are central, so a ban on intervention is rejected.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Mein Kampf chapter on Nation and Race describes the Jew as the attacker who works by lies, gains domination in the state and weaves a net of enemies around resisting peoples through his international influence.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Aryanism prizes marriage for racial reproduction, regulating it via the Nuremberg Laws, not abolishing it.

local-production.rationale: Blood-and-soil rhetoric favoured peasant agriculture, but the doctrine is silent on local production in general.

informal-organisation.rationale: Aryanism demands a hierarchical, leader-led structure, opposing informal horizontal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Hitler placed the racial state above international law and treaties.

religious-nation.rationale: Aryanism defines the nation by race, not religion; Hitler was wary of religious definitions.

defeat-communism.rationale: Nazi racial theory cast Bolshevism as a Jewish-led threat to be destroyed.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Nazi practice persecuted homosexual men under Paragraph 175, and the racial state treated them as a threat to Aryan reproduction.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects democracy and the Nazi state eliminated opposition parties and independent organisations to preserve racial unity.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Nazi doctrine was racial, not religious; sources say little on punishing blasphemy and adherents split between Christian, pagan and secular views.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Aryanism holds the Aryan race entitled to rule other races, and Lebensraum treated conquered lands as serving the master race.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Mein Kampf and Gobineau reject democracy and equality, and hold decisions rest with the racial elite under the leader.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The doctrine holds that races are fixed and unequal and rejects the idea of overlapping oppressions needing joint remedy.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Nazi doctrine invoked Providence, but authority was held to come from the race and the Fuhrer; adherents split between Christian, pagan and secular views.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Struggle between races and the state's duty to preserve the race make disarmament contrary to the doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Nazi Germany pursued alliances and expansion, and Mein Kampf favours alliances with chosen powers, so neutrality between blocs is not endorsed.

property-franchise.rationale: The racial doctrine makes blood, not property, the basis of citizenship and political rights, so a wealth qualification is not central.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Aryanism asserts hierarchy and natural struggle as good, and assigned women to a subordinate reproductive role.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist analysis; Nazi theory rejected Marxism and explained social conflict in racial terms.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Nazi legal order subordinated law to racial will and Fuhrer decrees and rejected equality before the law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Aryanism holds that only members of the racial community may be citizens with political rights, as in the Nuremberg Laws, and that the Aryan race should rule others.

online-participation.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about online deliberation, consultation or political participation in general, not voting, and the statement now asks whether citizens should have the option to vote online in public elections.

reviewHistory.rationale: The doctrine rejects mass deliberative democracy in favour of leader rule; online forums are used by modern adherents but not endorsed as decision-making.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Nazi boycott of Jewish shops in April 1933 was a signature early act of racial persecution, though the target was defined racially rather than religiously.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nazi racial doctrine denied non-Aryans any political voice, and the foreign-born even less.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Nazi practice built the Hitler Youth to train racially selected youth for national service.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Nazi racism denied the genocide of Jews, and neo-Nazi successors do the same.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Mein Kampf treats struggle and the right of the stronger as natural law, so abstaining from force is condemned.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Mein Kampf and Gobineau trace a continuous racial inheritance from the original Aryan stock to the present nation.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Gobineau's racial science treats sex and race as fixed biological facts, not constructs.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nazi practice built a cult of its dead as martyrs, and neo-Nazis keep up the memorials.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mein Kampf frames history as a struggle between the Aryan and its enemy, often in near-religious language.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Racial doctrine demands that economy and rule rest in Aryan hands and that Jews and other groups be excluded.

person-over-state.rationale: Hitler describes the state as a means to preserve the racial community, and individuals are subordinate to it.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mein Kampf treats races as locked in natural struggle and urges the Aryan to organise to defend and advance his race.

racial-pride.rationale: Aryanism holds the Aryan race to be superior and its preservation to be a duty.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mein Kampf calls for territorial expansion and conquest to secure living space for the race.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Hitler rejects language as the basis of nationhood and holds that blood and race, not speech, make a people.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on whether a foreign plot is believed to exist, or on foreign hostility in general rather than territorial partition, and the statement now asks whether preventing foreign-backed partition should be a central aim of national policy.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nazi doctrine cast Germany as threatened by a Jewish world conspiracy and by hostile encirclement.

arms-reduction.rationale: Racial struggle and conquest of living space are central; Mein Kampf treats armed strength as necessary and disarmament as weakness.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Nazi state disarmed opponents and 'unreliable' groups while the party's own armed formations served the regime, so a state-controlled armed monopoly under racial rule is the expected position.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Racial struggle and war are glorified and obedience is central, so refusing orders to fight is rejected.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The racial doctrine does not address income top-ups; Nazi welfare favoured racially valued families but no tax-credit position is documented.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: A fixed racial order enforced by the state leaves no room for communities choosing their own systems.

sacred-nation.rationale: Mein Kampf treats the racial nation (Volk) as the bearer of culture whose preservation is the highest duty, outlasting its members.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Aryanism holds that races differ in biological worth and rejects a common human nature and equal dignity.

public-service-media.rationale: Nazi Germany used media as state propaganda under Goebbels, not as independent public service media.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Aryanism rejects democracy and equality in favour of rule by the racially superior and a leader principle, so procedure alone confers no legitimacy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Nazi practice mixed moral conservatism with pronatalism for racially valued women; adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Aryanism holds that races are distinct biological categories with inherited hierarchy, the opposite of this statement, as the sources set out.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Mein Kampf treats the racial state as for the Aryan nation and denies other races rights of their own territory within it.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Nazi racial doctrine treated ethnic Germans abroad as part of the racial community whose interests the state should serve.

self-ownership.rationale: Mein Kampf subordinates the individual to the race and state, which can demand body and labour.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The doctrine treats race as the decisive force in history, so racial matters are central, though it frames the disadvantaged group differently from the statement's intent.

multipolar-world.rationale: Aryanism sought German or Aryan racial dominance, not a balance of equal powers, though some later neo-Nazis favour separate racial blocs; adherents differ.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Nazi national socialism joined nation and 'Aryan' workers, but denied international worker solidarity; the statement's second half conflicts.

material-over-identity.rationale: Racial identity is the core of the doctrine and is placed above class and material interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The doctrine rejects socialism and communism and has no communist party leadership of a market.

police-more-powers.rationale: Racial struggle, conquest and enforcement of racial laws required a strong military and police apparatus. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Some races are inherently superior to others and are entitled to rule them.
missingStatements.rationale: The core claim of Aryanism is that the Aryan race is superior and entitled to rule other peoples.

missingStatements.text: The mixing of races causes the decline of civilizations.
missingStatements.rationale: Gobineau and Hitler both attribute the fall of civilizations to racial mixing or blood poisoning.

missingStatements.text: Jews are a distinct race whose influence harms the nations they live among.
missingStatements.rationale: Hitler calls Jews a parasitic race and Nazi ideology treated them as the main threat to Aryans.
missingStatements.declined: Targets one specific group, which would only suit a few ideologies; the racial-hierarchy and race-mixing statements already capture the underlying racial doctrine.

notes: Gobineau himself wrote positively of Jews and saw decline as unavoidable, and Italian fascists used a Mediterranean version of 'Aryan'; neither matches the Nazi-era profile. Many non-racial questions (economy, religion) are unaddressed and answered from Nazi practice at low confidence.
